checks.claim: A photoelectric smoke detector shines a light beam away from a sensor; smoke scatters the light onto the sensor and sets off the alarm.
checks.why: The LED and the sensor sit at an angle so the beam misses the sensor; smoke particles scatter part of it onto the sensor, and past a threshold the horn sounds.

sources.title: How Do Smoke Detectors Work? (Live Science)

checks.claim: Smoke alarms must sound at least 85 decibels at 10 feet.
checks.why: NFPA 72 / UL 217: residential smoke alarms sound at 85 dBA measured at 10 feet; manufacturer sheets list at least 85 dB at 10 ft.

checks.claim: Fire safety agencies say to test smoke alarms once a month by pressing the test button.
checks.why: NFPA and fire departments say to test smoke alarms at least monthly by pushing the test button.
